AgentBucket.description:
One agent's slice of the org's traffic.

Named for agents-as-bots. Not to be confused with `AgentPerformanceBucket`, which is one
human teammate's inbox workload — the two words collide in this product and the
endpoints (`/by-agent` vs `/agents`) are deliberately spelled differently because of it.
AgentBucket.title: AgentBucket

AgentPerformanceBucket.description:
One human teammate's inbox workload.

Distinct from the per-channel breakdown: this reports on *people*, not surfaces.
Durations are None rather than 0 when there's nothing to average — a teammate who has
never resolved anything hasn't achieved a 0ms resolution time.
AgentPerformanceBucket.title: AgentPerformanceBucket

AgentTemplateOut.description: A creation-time starting point. Static catalog data — not per-org, never persisted.
AgentTemplateOut.title: AgentTemplateOut

AttachedAgent.description: An agent whose RAG config points at this knowledge base.
AttachedAgent.title: AttachedAgent

AttentionItemOut.description:
A row in the Attention queue.

Carries the whole flag history rather than just the current level, because the trajectory
is what an operator triages on: three flags in four minutes reads very differently from one
flag an hour ago, and the current level alone cannot show that.
AttentionItemOut.title: AttentionItemOut

AutomationBindingOut.description: One Vicero tool pointing at this workflow.
AutomationBindingOut.title: AutomationBindingOut

AutomationOut.description: One n8n workflow, resolved to its owning org via its tags.
AutomationOut.title: AutomationOut

ChannelBucket.description:
One channel's slice of the overview.

Every channel the org has *connected* gets a bucket, including ones with no traffic
yet — a freshly-connected WhatsApp should read as a real zero, not vanish from the
breakdown. Rates are 0.0 on zero conversations (the UI renders that as an em dash,
since 0% resolution would read as failure rather than "nothing happened yet").
ChannelBucket.title: ChannelBucket

ContactOut.description: The human on the other end — what the inbox needs to render a recognizable row.
ContactOut.title: ContactOut

ConversationFlagOut.description: One reason a human was asked to look.
ConversationFlagOut.title: ConversationFlagOut

CreateContactRequest.description: Operator-created contact — the one path into the CRM that isn't a chat message.
CreateContactRequest.title: CreateContactRequest

CreateDocumentRequest.description: Add a document from raw text or a URL (file uploads use the /upload endpoint).
CreateDocumentRequest.title: CreateDocumentRequest

CurrencyTotalsOut.description:
This calendar month's ledger for ONE currency. Amounts are minor units of `currency`; a
row exists per currency present, and no field ever combines two currencies.
CurrencyTotalsOut.title: CurrencyTotalsOut

DayPoint.description:
One calendar day of activity.

Distinct from `UsageBucket` because a chart and a usage table want different things.
`UsageBucket` is sparse — it only has rows for days that saw traffic — which is correct
for a table and wrong for a time series: plotting sparse points by array index spaces
Jul 30, Aug 2 and Aug 6 evenly and draws a straight line through a month of silence.
Every day in the range gets a point here, zeros included.

`conversations` counts conversations *started* that day, which is what "conversations
per day" means to an operator. The chart previously plotted assistant message count,
since that was the only per-day number the API had.
DayPoint.title: DayPoint

EntitlementsOut.description:
`GET /v1/me/entitlements` (docs/22 §8.1) — what this org may do right now, plus usage.

For rendering only, never for a security decision: every limit here is re-enforced
server-side at the point of mutation, so a client that lies about this response still gets
a 402. Deliberately carries **no payment information** — `payment_state`/`billing_cycles`
are staff-only (docs/22 §5.1 rule 1); this answers "what can I do", not "have I paid".
EntitlementsOut.title: EntitlementsOut

ExpectedToolCall.title: ExpectedToolCall

InvitationLinkOut.description:
A freshly minted acceptance link for a pending invitation.

Invitation tokens are stored hashed, so the original link cannot be read back — issuing one
necessarily mints a new token and **invalidates any link already sent**. Callers must say so.
InvitationLinkOut.title: InvitationLinkOut

InvitationPreview.description:
What an invitation says, readable without redeeming it.

Lets the accept page name the org and role, prefill the invited address, and open in the
right mode instead of defaulting to signup and failing for anyone who already has an account.

`account_exists` tells a token holder whether that address is registered. They already hold a
single-use token that was emailed to it, so this is not an enumeration oracle — but it is a
disclosure, which is why the route is rate-limited and returns the same opaque
`org.invitation_invalid` for a spent, revoked, expired or fabricated token.
InvitationPreview.title: InvitationPreview

LinkedChannelOut.title: LinkedChannelOut

MacroAction.description:

N8nSignatureFindingOut.title: N8nSignatureFindingOut

OrgMemberOut.title: OrgMemberOut

PackOut.description: One `pack_added` grant, for the admin panel's Uninvoiced packs reconciliation view.
PackOut.title: PackOut

PlanFeaturesOut.description: On/off capabilities, derived from the counts above (docs/22 §4.1).
PlanFeaturesOut.title: PlanFeaturesOut

PlanLimitsOut.description: Caps for one plan. `None` means unlimited; `0` means the feature is not included.
PlanLimitsOut.title: PlanLimitsOut

PlanStatusOut.title: PlanStatusOut

PricingOut.description:
The pricing page's entire data source.

`contact_only` is true while plans are granted by staff rather than bought self-serve
(docs/22 §1) — the page renders "Contact us", not "Buy". It flips when docs/23 ships.
PricingOut.title: PricingOut

ProviderKeyUpsert.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/credentials/providers/{name}` — one key per provider.

The Settings page presents providers, not credential rows: an operator clicks a provider
and types a key. Re-saving replaces the key in place instead of stacking a second row that
`resolve_credential()` would then have to arbitrate between.
ProviderKeyUpsert.title: ProviderKeyUpsert

ScriptedNodeOutputs.description:
Cached-mode script (ADR-081): canned outputs for `tool`/`agent`/`sub_agent` nodes, keyed
by what each node type's real executor callback actually receives — a graph node_id is
never passed to an executor, so it cannot be the key here.
ScriptedNodeOutputs.title: ScriptedNodeOutputs

SendWindowOut.description: Platform limits on replying right now. Null on channels that impose none.
SendWindowOut.title: SendWindowOut

TimeseriesPoint.description:
One bucket of the dashboard "Activity" bar chart (docs/20 §9.3.2, ADR-101).

`bucket_start` is the *local* calendar date the bucket starts on (the Monday of a week,
the 1st of a month) — local to the `tz` the request was made with, not UTC, so a bar
labelled "Sep 28" really is everything the caller's midnight-to-midnight Sep 28 contained.
TimeseriesPoint.title: TimeseriesPoint

TimeseriesResponse.description:
`GET /v1/analytics/timeseries` (ADR-101): one metric, zero-filled, bucketed by the
caller's timezone, plus the same-length prior period's total for the header's delta pill.
TimeseriesResponse.title: TimeseriesResponse

TodaySnapshot.description:
Conversations in a caller-supplied window, split into exactly three buckets
(docs/20-UI-REDESIGN-DUAL-THEME.md's dashboard "Today" gauge; ADR-100).

The window is the *caller's* local day, not the server's: the frontend computes
`start`/`end` from the browser's own midnight-to-now (or an org timezone, once one is
stored) and sends them as UTC instants, so this endpoint never has to guess a timezone.

A conversation lands in exactly one bucket:
- `resolved_by_ai` — no `Handoff` row at all; the bot handled it start to finish.
- `handed_to_human` — a `Handoff` row exists and a human has engaged (`assigned_to` is
  set, or its status is `resolved`).
- `unanswered` — a `Handoff` row exists but no human has picked it up yet.

`conversations == resolved_by_ai + handed_to_human + unanswered`, always.
TodaySnapshot.title: TodaySnapshot

ToolCallSpec.description:
One entry in a test case's cached-mode script — fed into
`app.llm.fake.MultiRoundToolProvider`.
ToolCallSpec.title: ToolCallSpec

UsageCountsOut.description:
Live counts for this org, same shape as `PlanLimitsOut` so the two compare directly —
but never `None`: a live count is always a number, unlike a cap.
UsageCountsOut.title: UsageCountsOut

WidgetCampaign.description: A proactive message the widget may show unprompted (see modules/campaigns).
WidgetCampaign.title: WidgetCampaign

WidgetTheme.description:
The widget's live config response. Every new field is optional/defaulted so an agent
that never touches the new controls renders exactly as it does today.
WidgetTheme.title: WidgetTheme

WorkflowApprovalOut.description:
A workflow paused on an Approval node, surfaced in the inbox (docs/17 Phase 2 item 4) —
the same `Handoff` model a chat escalation uses, read through a workflow-shaped lens.
WorkflowApprovalOut.title: WorkflowApprovalOut

WorkflowVersionDiffOut.description:
Structural diff between two versions of the same workflow's graph (docs/17 Phase 4) —
see `app.workflows.diff` for how each field is computed. Never a text/JSON diff: a node
whose config changed is reported separately from one that was added or removed.
WorkflowVersionDiffOut.title: WorkflowVersionDiffOut

get.description:
The pricing table, rendered from `app.core.plans.PLANS`, in USD, EUR or INR.

The marketing page must call this rather than hardcoding numbers, so a plan change is one
edit in `plans.py` and never a stale price on a public page.

The currency is **display only** (see `app.core.geo`): `?currency=` wins, then a country
header (only when `TRUST_GEO_HEADERS`), then USD. An unsupported `?currency=` is ignored.
Because the body varies by country, the response is `Cache-Control: private` and lists the
geo headers in `Vary`, so a shared cache can never hand the INR list to a German visitor.
